rmt-2014-team-02.title: Exponent mod 4
rmt-2014-team-02.body:
The last digit of $2^E$ ($E\ge1$) cycles $2,4,8,6$ with period $4$ in $E$, so we need $E\bmod4$ where $E=3^{k}$ and $k=4^{(\cdots)}$ is even. Since $3\equiv-1\pmod4$, $3^k\equiv1\pmod 4$ for even $k$. So $E\equiv1\pmod4$ and the last digit is that of $2^1$, namely $2$.

**Answer: 2**
